sections.text: We identify the search intent behind each page, then refine the title, content and internal links so visitors find their answer and move on to the next step.

sections.title: Every element on the page serves the visitor's question
sections.text: A good page isn't a collection of keywords. It's a well-organized answer that takes visitors from their question to the next step.

items.heading: Search intent & keywords
items.label: We work out what a phrase really means and assign each keyword group to the one page that deserves it.

items.heading: Title & meta description
items.label: A title that matches the query and a description that makes the value clear, without stuffing or repetition.

items.heading: Content structure
items.label: Ordering headings and paragraphs so visitors quickly reach what they're looking for.

items.heading: Internal links
items.label: Linking each page to the pages that support it and the pages it leads to, to distribute importance across the site.

items.heading: Keyword cannibalization
items.label: Merging or separating pages that compete with each other for the same phrase.

items.heading: Structured data
items.label: Schema suited to the page type that clarifies its content for search engines.

sections.title: What you get from an on-page SEO project

items.label: A keyword and page map showing which page owns each search intent.
Updated titles and meta descriptions for priority pages.
A proposed content structure for each page that needs reorganizing.
An internal linking plan between service and content pages.
A list of competing pages, with a merge-or-separate decision for each.

items.question: What's the difference between on-page SEO and technical SEO?
items.answer: Technical SEO deals with search engines' ability to reach and read a page, while on-page SEO deals with what's on the page itself: search intent, title, content and links.

items.question: How do you know if two pages are competing with each other?
items.answer: We check in Search Console which pages appear for the same phrase and keep swapping positions, then decide whether to merge them or separate the intent between the two.

items.question: Do you rewrite page content?
items.answer: We reorganize the content and add what's missing. Writing new pages from scratch falls under our SEO content service.

items.question: How many pages do you work on each month?
items.answer: It depends on the scope of work and the condition of the pages. We start with the pages closest to generating orders, then expand from there.

items.question: Do I need a developer?
items.answer: Most changes are made directly in your platform. We only need your developer for templates and custom-built systems.
